title: Robustness of Off-Axis Electron Vortices in Nonuniform Magnetic Fields
authors: Hui-Dong Huang, Qi Meng, Zhi-Bin Wang, Liang Lu, Jian Chen, Li-Ping Zou
abstract: Rotational symmetry protects the topological charge of on-axis electron vortices but not of off-axis vortices. We identify an additional SU(1,1) dynamical invariant that guarantees conservation of their intrinsic orbital angular momentum within the near-axis approximation. First-principles simulations of an off-axis electron vortex traversing a Glaser lens confirm this prediction, establishing a robust transport mechanism in axisymmetric nonuniform magnetic fields.
summary: This paper analyzes the conservation of intrinsic orbital angular momentum for electron vortices moving off-axis through magnetic lenses. The authors prove that this conservation is guaranteed by a hidden SU(1,1) dynamical invariant, even when simple symmetries are broken. This finding is confirmed via detailed theoretical derivations and robust 3D numerical simulations.
main_problem: The study investigates how the intrinsic orbital angular momentum (OAM) of off-axis electron vortices is conserved when propagating through nonuniform magnetic fields, contrasting this with on-axis cases protected by rotational symmetry.
main_result: The intrinsic OAM is found to be robustly conserved due to a hidden SU(1,1) dynamical invariant, which is confirmed by both theoretical derivation in the paraxial limit and high-fidelity 3D numerical simulations.
method: The work combines analytical derivations using Hamiltonian mechanics (Heisenberg equations of motion) with advanced numerical techniques like operator-splitting Fourier pseudo-spectral methods to simulate wavepacket evolution.
model_or_system: The system models an electron vortex propagating in a magnetic field, specifically utilizing the Glaser lens profile $B(z) = B_0(1 + z^2/a^2)^{-1}$. The dynamics are governed by the time-dependent Schrödinger equation with a vector potential $\mathbf{A}$.
key_observables: Intrinsic Orbital Angular Momentum ($L_i$), Extrinsic OAM ($L_{	ext{ext}}$), and the conserved SU(1,1) norm.
important_parameters: Magnetic field variation scale ($a$), initial transverse offset ($y_0$), and topological charge ($\ell$).
main_assumptions: The theoretical proof relies on the paraxial approximation, although numerical results suggest robustness beyond this limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate off-axis vortex propagation through a magnetic lens, showing centroid trajectories and confirming that $L_i$ remains nearly constant despite field gradients and initial offsets.
paper_structure: The paper develops the Hamiltonian formalism for electron dynamics in nonuniform fields, derives equations of motion for expectation values (including $L_{	ext{ext}}$), identifies the hidden SU(1,1) invariant, and validates this conservation law through both analytical proofs and extensive 3D numerical simulations.
why_interesting: The discovery of a non-obvious dynamical symmetry (SU(1,1)) protecting a key quantum observable ($L_i$) in a complex physical setting like nonuniform fields is highly relevant for understanding topological robustness in wave propagation.
